root_cause.text: In `drivers/iommu/generic_pt/iommu_pt.h`, `iommupt_unmap_pages()` flushed only the originally requested `len` instead of the actual `unmap.unmapped` span, so when unmapping crossed into a large/contiguous IOPTE and removed more than requested, the IOTLB gather/invalidation covered too short a range.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, len, ...)` to `gather_range_pages(iotlb_gather, iommu_table, iova, unmap.unmapped, ...)`, and the commit message explicitly says unmap can “unmap more than requested” in this case and the gather was “only flushing the range requested to be unmapped, not extending to the extra range,” causing a “short invalidation.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the actual unmapped length when gathering range pages after unmapping.
intent_record.what: The call to `gather_range_pages()` in `DOMAIN_NS(unmap_pages)` was changed so that its fourth argument is `unmap.unmapped` instead of `len`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the page-gathering logic now operates on the actual number of bytes/pages that were successfully unmapped rather than on the original requested length. This makes the IOTLB/page bookkeeping consistent with partial unmaps and prevents gathering more range pages than were actually unmapped.

grouping_result.intent: Use the actual unmapped length when gathering range pages after unmapping.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it changes the unmap flush/gather logic to use the actual unmapped length instead of the originally requested length, fixing the too-short IOTLB invalidation range.

candidates.rationale: This uses the originally requested len for IOTLB gathering after unmapping, instead of the actual unmapped span (unmap.unmapped). If the unmap removes more than requested due to a large/contiguous IOPTE, the flush range is too short.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement passes the originally requested len to gather_range_pages() after unmapping, so the IOTLB flush covers only the requested length instead of the actual unmapped span (unmap.unmapped). That can leave part of a larger contiguous IOPTE mapping unflushed when more pages were actually unmapped.
